key_findings: WAL still permits only one writer at a time; canonical writers must not be modeled as parallel simply because readers and writers can overlap.
WAL readers use snapshot isolation; a long-lived read transaction can be stale and read-to-write escalation can fail with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT.
Long-lived/overlapping readers can starve checkpoints and grow the WAL; reader lifetime and checkpoint progress should be observable.
WAL is same-host shared-memory coordination, not a distributed/multi-host state mechanism.
synchronous=NORMAL weakens power-loss durability relative to FULL and must not silently receive stronger canonical-state durability credit.

SQLite documents a rare concurrent WAL reset/checkpoint corruption race affecting 3.7.0 through 3.51.2, fixed in 3.51.3+ and listed fixed backports 3.44.6/3.50.7; actual target runtime SQLite version remains unobserved.
